candidates.rationale: Wide intraday range relative to the stock's own opening price, arriving with dollar volume well above its own six-month norm, marks broad-participation repricing rather than a thin air-pocket, and turnover-validated moves keep extending as slower participants catch up.

A stock whose daily dollar turnover rises specifically alongside its own same-day gains rather than its losses shows price strength that real buying flow is confirming, and demand-confirmed moves tend to keep extending.

Dollar volume measured against a recency-weighted two-week baseline catches a still-building surge in participation before a flat moving average would, and when that surge coincides with a positive five-day return it looks demand-driven and likely to continue.

An open-to-high rally matters more when it rides volume that ranks unusually high within the stock's own recent history, so ranking the percentage move together with the stock's own 42-day volume percentile isolates rallies with real, historically-unusual participation behind them.

The number of the past two weeks that a stock's dollar turnover ran above its own quarterly norm measures whether an attention surge has been sustained rather than a one-day spike, and sustained participation paired with the concurrent two-week return marks a trend built on durable flow.

Dollar volume that has structurally grown versus where it stood two quarters ago, on a day the stock also posts a wide absolute trading range, shows both the participation and the actual price-discovery of a re-rating already in motion, not quiet volume growth that hasn't moved the stock yet.

When a stock's same-day price move ranks far higher across the market than its own dollar volume ranks within its own trailing month, the move lacked the participation to back it, a fragile dislocation that tends to partially reverse once ordinary two-sided volume returns.

Information diffuses more slowly through a thinly-traded name's holder base, so an existing multi-week trend has further to run in the low-dollar-volume tier than in a heavily-watched, high-turnover name where the same move is already fully arbitraged.

Weighting the past month's daily ranges by recency instead of averaging them flatly, then comparing that to the stock's plain quarterly average range, isolates a liquidity/volatility regime that is still actively widening from one that already peaked and is fading back to normal.

Time since a stock's own most recent quarterly peak in dollar volume marks how long it has been since its last broad liquidity event, and pairing that recency with the return accumulated over the same window turns the drift since that event, continuation or reversal, into a single score.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. A 252-day window on volume or dollar volume dropped coverage to exactly 0.874 in both instances this round, just under the 0.90 floor, while 63-day windows on the same fields passed coverage fine; avoid 252-day volume windows.
  2. Changing only the lookback window on an already-archived expression (10 vs 21, or 63 vs 21) reliably triggers the correlation gate at rho 0.94 to 0.98; vary the functional form, not just window length, when building on archived structures.
  3. Raw dollar volume and its medium-window mean both duplicate the archived short-window dollar-volume mean at rho above 0.93; this normalizer is saturated, so pair dollar volume with a new signal rather than proposing it alone.
  4. All three accepts this round pair a price range (high-low or high-close distance) with a dollar-volume or liquidity-rank normalizer, spanning fast, medium, and slow speed niches; this structure is currently the productive one, favor it over fundamentals crossovers.
  5. A near-duplicate of the round's top accepted factor, differing by one normalizer swap, was rejected for sharing 5 nodes with it; edits to a freshly-accepted winner need a different normalizer or range definition, not a single-node swap, to count as novel.
  6. 8 of 9 archive_subtree rejections this round were a single local edit to an already-archived expression with everything else identical: swapping one price field (close for open), swapping the smoothing operator (EMA for a moving average), adding/removing an outer wrapper (rank, lag, or an extra smoothing layer), or inserting a short moving-average around one existing raw term. A single-point edit isn't enough to clear the subtree gate: change two or more structural elements at once, or change the combining operator itself.
  7. Volume/dollar-volume expressions built only from level, threshold-count, rank-difference, or delta transforms (no price-range or return term) failed the cheap screen 4 times this round (t 0.43-0.88). The one pure-volume shape that passed was a dispersion ratio (std over mean of dollar volume): favor dispersion over level/count/rank-diff/delta when a factor has no price or return term.
  8. Combining a raw (unranked) mean-return with a time-series-ranked liquidity measure, either by multiplying them or by using volume as an on/off filter for the return, produced very weak fitness (t=0.67 and t=0.05). Rank each side cross-sectionally before combining rather than mixing a raw term with a ranked one.
  9. Weighting an existing up/down-day count by volume (summing volume on positive-return days) reproduced the plain unweighted count almost exactly (rho=0.881 against the archived count factor). Volume-weighting a counting factor is not a reliable way to diversify it.
  10. Two rejections this round were exact duplicates of proposals already made earlier in the same run (a single fundamental ratio, a close-based range normalization). Check a candidate against this run's own proposal list before spending a generation call on it.
  11. This round's accepted factors took two shapes: a pure dollar-volume dispersion ratio, and two factors pairing a range/spread term (high-low, high-open, or open-low) with dollar-volume via a cross-sectional rank product or a rank-difference, never a plain ratio of the two. Plain ratio-of-two-raw-terms variants in the spread/dollar-volume family are archive-saturated; the rank-product and rank-difference shapes are not.
  12. A crossover call failed outright this round from exceeding the output token cap, losing that paid call for nothing. Bias crossover toward smaller/shallower parent-tree pairs so the combined output stays in budget.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
